the effects of sample size and construct reliability (p/f and factor loading magnitude) on model fit and parameter estimation in confirmatory factor models.
the extent to which sample size affects the quality of parameter estimates in CFA models.
the question: What is the minimum sample size required for the accurate estimation of the parameters of a given model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sample size should be large enough to provide a good fit of a model that has a good measurement model quality.
the sample size should not be too small, and it should not be too large.
sample size recommendations should be made in terms of construct reliability and n, not in terms of p/f, number of factors, or number of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more reliable the measurement model, the smaller the sample size that is necessary to achieve accurate parameter estimates and to ensure model convergence.
researchers need to consider the number of indicators for each factor and the number of factors when determining the appropriate sample size for CFA.
the more complex the measurement model, the larger the sample size needed for convergence and accurate parameter estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should consider the quality of measurement models in their research designs and in their interpretation of results.
the number of observations per variable (N/PV) is a critical design feature that must be considered in CFA.
the quality of measurement model (as indexed by construct reliability) is more important than sample size in determining the quality of CFA results.
